----Respondent
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Hitendra Singh
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Deepak Choudhary, Aag
 Mr. Kuldeep Singh, Aaag
 Ms. Anju Gurjar
 Mr. Bhawani Singh Ransi
Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sandeep Shah (Vacation Judge)
Order 04/06/2025
1.

This application for bail under Section 483 B.N.S.S. has been filed by the petitioner who has been
arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.30/2025 registered at Police Station Sajjangarh, District
Banswara for the offences punishable under Sections 376 and 420 of Ipc and Sections 67 and 67(k)
of Information Technology Act.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the allegations leveled against the petitioner are totally frivolous and it is a case of love relationship gone soar.
It is further submitted that post getting engaged with the prosecutrix, she alleged that the petitioner had an ex-lover and for this reason alone, the FIR in question has been lodged.

It has further been submitted that the [2025:RJ-JD:26813] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-5875/2025] prosecutrix has voluntarily accepted the fact that both of them stayed together in a hotel at Jaipur way back in the month of June 2024 and only for the reason that now the prosecutrix is having a doubt on petitioner having a relationship with someone else, the FIR in question has been lodged.
4. The counsel further submitted that no recovery is due to be made from the present petitioner, and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time.

Therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to Vishal vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:26813) on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159310711/
1 the accused-petitioner.

5. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor, as well as the learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that while the petitioner and the prosecutrix stayed at a hotel in Jaipur, the petitioner tried to take benefit of the situation and indulged in sexual acts with the prosecutrix.

It has further been asserted that post the relationship gone soar, the petitioner posted certain unwanted contents in a group chat of the members of the community in question and therefore, it is contended that this is not a fit case for the grant of bail.
6.
Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that the prosecutrix and the petitioner were engaged and stayed together.

The alleged incident pertains to the month of June 2024, when the prosecutrix and the petitioner were engaged and also considering the fact that post the relationship having gone soar due to alleged love affair of petitioner with some other girl, the present FIR has [2025:RJ-JD:26813] (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-5875/2025] been lodged, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
7.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 B.N.S.S. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Vishal S/o Govind arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.30/2025 registered at Police Station Sajjangarh, District Banswara, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
8. It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.

(SANDEEP SHAH (VACATION JUDGE)),J 133-Love/-
